text:
The fog did not merely obscure the station; it consumed it. At midnight, the air hung heavy and wet, tasting of iron and damp wool. The platform lights buzzed with a dying electrical hum, casting sickly yellow pools that fractured against the encroaching mist. Snowflakes, if they were snow, dissolved before touching the ground, turning into a slick, freezing film on the slate tiles.

I stood beneath the canopy, collar turned up, watching the empty tracks vanish into the grey void. There was no sound but the rhythmic *tick-tick* of the cooling engine from a long-departed freight train, echoing like a slow heartbeat in the throat of the valley. The bench beside me was glazed with ice, reflecting my own pale, distorted face. Time felt suspended here, caught between the last train’s whistle and the first breath of dawn. I waited for a signal that never came, wrapped in the silence so thick it pressed against my eardrums, a cold companion in the dark.
